transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-29
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Aegis CTO), Liam O'Connor (Security Architect), Rachel Kim (Cloud Infra Lead), Marco Ruiz (Compliance)

AutoSummary: quick deep dive focused on private/VPC deployment and network security.

[00:00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll run about an hour, high level then Samir will go into the architecture. 
[00:00:10] Priya (Aegis CTO): thanks, jordan. quick note - we're evaluating Private deployment because of residency and regulated data lines, so want to understand ingress, egress, and how audit logs get out to our SIEM.
[00:00:22] Samir (Redwood SE): great, yeah we'll cover three major areas: network isolation and routing, ingress/egress and firewalling, and then encryption/KMS + audit pipelines. i have a sample terraform diagram i'll reference.
[00:00:35] Liam (Aegis SecArch): quick callout - our security bar requires customer-managed keys for long-term storage and tamper-evident audit trails. also we need SSO integration and RBAC mapping to groups.
[00:00:48] Jordan: noted. samir, take it away.

[00:01:05] Samir: alright starting with the high level - two deployment models we recommend: private VPC deployment where Redwood control plane is managed but the inference nodes live in your VPC via a private connector; or fully on-premised package for air-gapped setups. the VPC option supports private endpoints and no public internet egress for the inference nodes if you configure NAT gateways and egress proxies appropriately.
[00:01:30] Rachel (Aegis): when you say control plane managed, what data flows out? we need to limit any PII leaving the VPC.
[00:01:40] Samir: good question. in the private control plane model the control plane talks to agents in your VPC for orchestration only; customer can opt to disable telemetry and logs to Redwood's SaaS and instead stream audit events to your SIEM. payloads stay in the VPC when configured - we support PrivateLink-style endpoints and mutual TLS. there are two patterns: 1) outbound-only control channel from nodes to control plane over TLS with strict IP allowlists, or 2) fully offline on-prem package where no outbound is allowed.
[00:02:15] Liam: how do you enforce network isolation internally? like, can we put inference nodes in isolated private subnets with no public IPs?
[00:02:24] Samir: yes. recommended topology: separate subnets per function - inference workers in private subnets (no public IP), management agents in a restricted management subnet, and a bastion or jump box in a hardened admin subnet. security groups restrict ports (only 443 to control plane or to your egress proxy), NACLs for additional layer-of-defense, and explicit route tables to ensure no unintended internet traffic. we also recommend flow logs at subnet level.
[00:02:52] Priya: what about egress filtering? we have strict egress controls - only allowed to go through our egress proxy to the internet.
[00:03:00] Samir: supported. we can route control plane traffic to an internal egress proxy, and the inference workload itself doesn't need outbound internet unless you enable model downloads from public repos. model artifacts can be pre-seeded into the cluster from an internal artifact repo or S3 bucket via signed URLs - that avoids node-level outbound.
[00:03:20] Marco (Compliance): audit logs - we need tamper-evident retention for seven years and integration with Splunk. how does Redwood support that?
[00:03:28] Samir: we provide audit event streaming via syslog/HTTPS to your SIEM. events are signed at generation with a key you control if you use BYOK; we also support writing logs to an encrypted S3 bucket in your account with server-side encryption using your KMS key. for tamper-evidence we recommend immutable S3 object lock plus periodic signed manifests.
[00:03:50] Liam: can we host the KMS in our HSM? we need FIPS 140-2 validated HSM backed keys.
[00:03:57] Samir: yes, BYOK is supported. two options: integrate with cloud KMS where keys are customer-managed (AWS KMS CMKs) and optionally backed by CloudHSM; or for on-prem we can integrate with your HSM via KMIP or use a Redwood-hosted HSM peered over a private connection. the crypto operations for tokenization and storage are always performable with customer keys in the recommended model.
[00:04:20] Priya: and rotation? key rotation windows?
[00:04:24] Samir: we support key rotation policies; you can rotate CMKs on your schedule. for long-term encrypted objects we use envelope encryption so data keys rotate transparently while the master CMK rotates per your policy.

[00:04:45] Jordan: i want to pause and check off SSO and RBAC items. how does RBAC map to our IdP?
[00:04:52] Samir: SSO via SAML 2.0 or OIDC supported. Role mapping is configurable in the console; we can sync groups via SCIM so your IdP groups map to Redwood roles. for Private deployments you can host the console behind SSO as well, or integrate via your corporate proxy. we also support just-in-time provisioning.
[00:05:12] Rachel: for on-prem console access, can we bind to internal AD/LDAP?
[00:05:18] Samir: yes AD/LDAP integrations are possible for the on-prem packaged control plane. for the managed control plane we do SAML/OIDC and SCIM.

[00:05:35] [screen share: sample terraform diagram referenced by Samir]
[00:05:40] Samir: here's a sample terraform layout - VPC with three private subnets, NAT in a dedicated subnet with strict route tables, security groups for 443 inbound from specific management CIDRs, NACL explicit denies for risky ports, flow logs to our logging account or your SIEM. note the use of endpoint services - we suggest interface endpoints for S3, KMS, and control-plane API so traffic never traverses the public internet.
[00:06:10] Liam: do you have recommendations for firewall vendor integration? we use Palo Alto and Fortinet appliances on prem.
[00:06:17] Samir: yes, we commonly integrate with PAN-OS and FortiGate via egress proxy + IP allowlist and can provide example rules. for IPS/IDS we recommend tapping flow logs into your existing IDS and applying application-layer rules at the egress proxy.

[00:06:35] Priya: curious about model governance - if we do canary rollouts or A/B, are audit trails kept for which model served which request?
[00:06:43] Samir: yes each inference request is tagged with model id, version, route, and decision metadata; audit events for inference decisions can be emitted and sent to SIEM or retained in encrypted S3. these are configurable to avoid logging PII.

[00:06:58] Marco: is there a way to redact PII before logs leave the VPC? we want to avoid storing PII in logs by default.
[00:07:05] Samir: absolutely - you can configure data-masking at the agent level. we support pre-send filters and regex-based redaction rules, or you can route raw events to an internal processing lambda that scrubs before forwarding to Splunk.

[00:07:22] Jordan: switching to ingress - do you support private endpoints for client apps to call the model? or do clients have to go through Redwood-managed public gateways?
[00:07:32] Samir: we support private endpoints via PrivateLink or interface endpoints. client apps inside the same VPC or peered VPCs can call the service endpoint privately; for external clients you can front with your API gateway or VPN. we also support mTLS between clients and the inference gateway for mutual auth.
[00:07:52] Rachel: about firewalling - what ports need to be open?
[00:07:55] Samir: primarily 443 for control plane and data plane. management ports for SSH are only allowed to the bastion host with strict CIDR limits. healthcheck ports are private. model push or artifact downloads are over HTTPS to endpoints inside the network or through signed internal repos.

[00:08:15] [00:08:20] Priya: we have a question about data residency - we must keep data in eu-west-1 and never cross into other regions. can we pin deployments?
[00:08:27] Samir: yes you can pin model-serving clusters to a region and restrict routing policies. for the managed control plane we can provision regional control-plane endpoints or arrange data plane only in the specified region; for full assurance the on-prem package is the cleanest.

[00:08:45] Liam: incident response - if there's a suspicious request or exfil pattern, how do we detect and block?
[00:08:52] Samir: couple of mechanisms - real-time request sampling and anomaly detection hooks, integrate WAF rules at the ingress, and block at egress with policy automation. we emit security events to your SIEM and support webhooks to trigger automated firewall rule changes.

[00:09:12] Marco: governance - do you have SOC2/ISO artifacts for vendor review?
[00:09:17] Jordan: yes, we'll send the latest SOC 2 Type II report, ISO31000 summary, and our security questionnaire answers. note some items are redacted but we'll provide the attestations.
[00:09:28] Priya: timeline - our security review board meets 5/18. we need artifacts and network diagram before then.
[00:09:35] Jordan: noted, we'll prioritize.

[00:09:40] [deep technical exchange 00:09:40 - 00:35:00 where Samir walks through iptables, route policies, and an example NAT-less pattern]
[00:09:45] Samir: for high-security setups you can do NAT-less by using private S3 endpoints and pre-pushing images; the inference nodes never need direct internet. use security groups to restrict to internal artifact store. for egress monitoring you can ship VPC flow logs to your logging account and set retention/immutable policies.
[00:10:30] Priya: can we get a boiled-down checklist of required AWS resources and policies?
[00:10:36] Samir: yes - i'll produce a checklist: VPC subnet layout, route tables, security groups, NACL recommendations, interface endpoints for S3/KMS, IAM roles for agents, CloudWatch/flow log config, S3 bucket policy for server-side encryption with CMK, and Splunk syslog endpoint example.
[00:11:05] Liam: how does Redwood handle secret injection (API keys, model credentials) into nodes?
[00:11:10] Samir: secrets are provided via your cloud provider's secret manager (parameter store/secrets manager) or a Vault integration; we don't store plaintext keys in the node filesystem. the agent retrieves secrets over a short-lived session and caches in memory only. logs never persist secrets.
[00:11:30] Rachel: about observability - can we get per-token billing and trace info in our own systems?
[00:11:36] Jordan: yes metering can be emitted as events to your billing pipeline; for deeper traces we have hooks that export traces to your tracing backend. those exports can be restricted to metadata only.
[00:12:00] [00:12:00 - 00:34:30] (detailed Q&A continues: firewall rule examples, sample NACLs, and recommended healthcheck endpoints; discussion of patching cadence for inference nodes, canary deploy specifics, and rollback policies)
[00:34:40] Priya: on patching - what's your security patch cadence and can we control updates?
[00:34:46] Samir: default cadence is monthly security patching with emergency patches as needed. for Private on-prem you can opt to run updates on your schedule; for managed nodes we coordinate maintenance windows and provide pre-tested builds.
[00:35:10] Jordan: ok, we're coming up on time. quick recap before we close.
[00:35:18] Jordan: agreed items are - we'll send SOC2 artifacts and the whitepaper; samir will produce VPC terraform samples and the checklist; aegis will send the compliance checklist and required log fields; we'll schedule a pilot planning session for mid-May.
[00:35:35] Priya: sounds good. any blockers for us to start a pilot? cost is primary question but security is gating.
[00:35:44] Jordan: understood, we'll include a pricing estimate for Dedicated capacity vs Private pilot with baseline SLOs.
[00:35:55] Marco: small question - does Redwood support legal addendum for data processing agreements and breach notification SLAs?
[00:36:02] Jordan: yes standard DPA and we can negotiate breach notification timelines in the enterprise contract.
[00:36:20] [wrap up chatter and scheduling]
[00:36:30] Samir: i'll drop the terraform diagram and an example security group/nacl file in the follow-up note.
[00:36:35] Jordan: i'll send SOC2 and the contact for our compliance reviewer.
[00:36:40] Priya: thanks everyone, appreciate it.
[00:36:50] End of recording.

Notes on transcription quality: speaker overlap at times, a few words transcribed phonetically (e.g., "Sam'l" instead of SAML). references shared: https://redwood.example.com/security/whitepaper (shared post-call), sample terraform gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/vpc-sample (placeholder), SOC2 attestation PDF (attached).
